title: 20-minute home workout, no equipment
intro: This 20-minute routine trains your whole body using only your own bodyweight. Good for busy beginners who want to exercise in the living room.
muscles: Full body: legs, glutes, chest, arms, shoulders and core, plus heart stamina.
steps: Warm up for 3 minutes: walk on the spot, roll your shoulders and swing your arms.
Do 40 seconds work, 20 seconds rest for each move: squat, knee push-up, glute bridge, reverse lunge, plank.
That's 1 round (5 minutes). Repeat for 3 rounds.
Rest 1 minute between rounds if needed, and drink water.
Cool down for 2 minutes with thigh, chest and back stretches.
mistakes: Chasing speed until your form breaks down. Better to go slow and do it right.
Hips too high or sagging during the plank. Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Skipping the warm-up and cool-down to save time.
easier: Switch to 30 seconds work, 30 seconds rest, and do only 2 rounds. Push-ups can be done against a wall.
harder: Switch to 45 seconds work, 15 seconds rest, add a 4th round, or swap squats for jump squats if your knees are okay.
dose: 20 minutes, 3 times a week with a rest day in between. On other days you can go for a walk.
safety: Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or sharp joint pain. If you've just given birth, have high blood pressure or heart problems, get your doctor's clearance first.

faq.q: My house is small. Can I still do this?
faq.a: Yes. You only need space about the size of a prayer mat. All moves are done on the spot.

faq.q: When is the best time to do it?
faq.a: Any time you can repeat consistently. Morning before work or after the kids are asleep are popular choices.

faq.q: Do I need to eat before exercising?
faq.a: Not a must. If you're hungry or feel weak, have a light snack like a banana 30-60 minutes before. Avoid exercising right after a big meal.
